title: Correlation — spoken follow-up
situation: In a technical discussion, a request crosses HTTP and a database dependency. You must answer aloud accurately without overstating the evidence.
instructions: Say aloud how a single request is followed across the API and the database call that it triggers.

vocabulary.meaning: following one request across every component it touches, using an identifier that survives each hop
the point where a correlation identifier stops being propagated, after which two related events can no longer be linked

expectedElements: The origin of the identifier is stated
Its propagation across at least two components is described
One realistic way the chain breaks is named
modelAnswer: The identifier is created at the edge, when the request first arrives, and only if the caller did not already supply one. From there it travels in the request context to the handler, and into the database call as a tag on the command. So one identifier ties together the evidence from the incoming request, the work we did, and the query we issued. The chain breaks in one predictable place: any point where we start background work without carrying the context across, because the new task gets a fresh context and loses the identifier. That is where I would look first if two events refuse to correlate. Do we have background work in this path?
commonMistakes: Describing tracing without saying where the identifier originates
Omitting the propagation boundary where the chain actually breaks
variants: Answer again for a request that crosses a message queue rather than a database.
